There are no surprise extras halfway through, and no big deposit to hand over up front. I would rather do fewer roofs and do them properly than rush around patching things that need doing right.

faq.q: Do you take a deposit up front?
faq.a: We do not ask for a big deposit before we start. For most jobs you pay when the work is done and you are happy with it, and on a larger re-roof we can agree staged payments in writing. Your money is not sat with a stranger while you hope they come back.

faq.q: How do I know you are not going to disappear like the cowboys?
faq.a: You deal with Sean directly, he is on the roof himself, and he lives and works here in Stockport. There is a written fixed price with your name on it, so you always know exactly who you hired and what was agreed.

faq.q: Why are you not the cheapest quote I have had?
faq.a: The cheapest quote usually leaves something out, and you end up paying again when it leaks. We price the whole job properly, put it in writing, and stick to it. You pay once and the roof lasts.

faq.q: Can you do a full re-roof or just repairs?
faq.a: Full re-roofs and new roofs are the main work we do. If your roof is past patching we will strip it and re-roof it properly. If it only needs a small repair we will tell you that honestly, rather than sell you a new roof you do not need.
We roof across Stockport and the towns around it, including Cheadle, Bramhall and Marple. If you are just outside that, give us a ring and we will let you know if we can still help.

faq.q: Will the price change once you get started?
faq.a: No. The written price is the price, as long as the job is what we agreed at the survey. If we ever find something hidden once the old roof is off, we stop and talk to you before anything else is done or charged.

blog_posts.title: How to spot a roofing cowboy before you pay a deposit
blog_posts.excerpt: The warning signs that a roofer is going to take your money and vanish.
blog_posts.body:
The biggest warning sign is being asked for a large deposit before any work starts. A settled local roofer does not need your cash up front to buy materials for a normal job. If someone wants a big deposit and is vague about when they will actually start, walk away.

Ask for the price in writing. A cowboy will keep it verbal so the number can drift up once the old roof is off and you are committed. A written fixed price tells you the roofer has properly worked the job out, and it gives you something to hold them to.

Check they are a real person you can find. A local address, a name on the paperwork, and a roofer who is happy for you to see other roofs they have done are all good signs. If you cannot pin down who you are actually hiring, that is your answer.

blog_posts.title: Re-roof or repair: how to tell when patching is a waste of money
blog_posts.excerpt: When a repair is the sensible fix, and when you are just throwing money at a tired old roof.
blog_posts.body:
A repair makes sense when the roof is sound but one specific thing has gone wrong, like a slipped slate or storm damage in a single spot. If the structure and the covering are otherwise in good order, there is no need to spend on a full re-roof.

The trouble starts when a roof is near the end of its life and you keep paying for patch after patch. Each repair costs money, the leaks keep moving to a new spot, and within a few years you have spent a good chunk of what a proper re-roof would have cost, with the same old roof still over your head.

The honest test is whether the same roof keeps giving you trouble. If a roofer keeps coming back out, ask for a straight opinion on whether it is time to re-roof. A good one will tell you the truth, even when the bigger job is not the answer you were hoping for.
